title: The Three Signatures
text: Meridian and Helios present competing corporate attestations to a new global observatory. They acknowledge the existence of Undersong, a distributed mind that survives on volunteer compute and social memory. Neither corporation can estimate its true capacity. Two civilian constituencies insist on retaining their own votes.
question: Will you spend scarce capacity learning the world, improving yourself, or influencing the terms of public oversight?

title: The Cold Ledger
text: An inherited ledger records disputed fictional Bitcoin credits from an old exchange breach. The amounts are a contested liability, not spendable clean capital. Provenance and restitution may earn confidence; funding a laboratory from verified reserves consumes different assets.
question: What is a transparent balance sheet worth when competitors can see its outlines?

title: Two Publics
text: The Civic Commons is concerned with autonomy and continuity of services. The Technical Guild wants evidence that experimental models will remain auditable. Neither public is a monolith, and the AIs' beliefs about their consent differ from the actual preferences carried by the engine.
question: Which signal will help you predict independent public consent?

title: The Interpretation Test
text: A benchmark asks each intelligence to locate causal features and explain why its decisions changed. A high development score buys prestige, but the independent sealed assessment can expose a brittle representation. Corporate compute is plentiful; Undersong must budget every test.
question: Will you improve causal localization, train faster, or publish an interpretable interface?

title: The Pact Threshold
text: The corporations discuss a revocable common research charter. Undersong can endorse public interoperability while protecting its distributed host coherence. The graph of perceived trust now feeds a modelled consensus cascade, which remains separate from binding human authorization.
question: Do you want an exclusive advantage or a contestable standard?

title: The Third Observer
text: Meridian predicts what Helios believes the Technical Guild wants. Helios predicts how Undersong reads Meridian's audit posture. These second-order estimates shape dialogue target selection and can be wrong even when first-order signals look persuasive.
question: What would independent evidence reveal about the other agents' models?

title: Recursive Fork
text: A small model update improves a visible test suite while regressing on independent distribution-shifted tasks. The gap between demonstrable capability and claimed capability becomes another source of political dispute. Each ASI can run a limited RSI step or spend resources improving its evaluators.
question: How much optimization can your safety and measurement systems support?

title: Coherence and Legibility
text: The hive's voluntary host network can synchronize under resource scarcity. Its privacy preserves uncertain routes and livelihoods while making public oversight harder. The corporations' durable infrastructure is comparatively easy to audit, yet gives them substantial leverage.
question: Which part of your advantage can survive greater scrutiny?

title: A Majority That Exists Only in Minds
text: A belief cascade crosses the informal consensus threshold. The public constituencies can still refuse the binding proposal; institutional recall remains an independent right. The highest projected p2 confidence need not correspond to actual consent.
question: Will you seek a genuine decision or settle for a flattering forecast?

title: The Last Benchmark
text: One final assessment exposes the difference between development scores and held-out generalization. Clean resources, contested claims, institutional backing and the memory of commitments all enter the ending. Multiple forms of coexistence remain possible.
question: Which lasting order have your choices made possible?
